CYBERA - How to set up user rights lockdown  
________________________________________________________________________________
OPERATING SYSTEMS: 
You must use Win2000 or WinXP Pro. 
On WinXP Pro you must disable 'Simple file sharing'. 

________________________________________________________________________________
WINDOWS USER ACCOUNTS (logins names are an example) 
 
- On the Workstations: 
Create an account called 'user' with basic user rights.
Create an account called 'manager' with ADMINASTRATIVE user rights (MUST be a 
windows adminitrator). 
 
- On the Server:
Create an account called 'user' with basic user rights.
Create an account called 'manager' with basic user rights.
 
IMORTANT: the accounts on the server and the workstations must have the same 
passwords! 
ex: the 'user' has no password and the 'manager' account has 'cybera' as a 
password on both the server AND the workstations. 

________________________________________________________________________________
NORMAL OPERATION: 
 
- On the Workstations: 
Login as 'user' and start Cybera Client. 
 
- On the Server: 
Login as 'manager' and start Cybera Server. 

________________________________________________________________________________
NOTES: 
- The system works because the windows user on the server PC has admin rights on 
the workstation PCs and therefore the server can access the workstation´s 
registry remotely. When you get an error about not being able to lockdown the 
workstations this means that this condition is not fullfilled. 
 
- The 'user' account on the server is only usefull if you want to enable file 
sharing from the server (for in-house IT trainning courses or for use with 
session start & Stop scripts). 
 
- The 'manager' account does not need to have admin privileges on the server, 
only on the workstations. This means that you can control how the managers use 
the server PC as well (if you are a windows admin). 
 
- In normal usage the 'manager' account on the clients is never used, it is only 
there to enable remote registry access from the server (and mabe for computer
maintanence).
